formal_source_nodes.name: 601.2b
formal_source_nodes.rule: If the spell is modal, the player announces the mode choice (see rule 700.2). If the player making the mode choice needs to be targeted, the player casting the spell announces their choice of an appropriate player for each target required to make that choice, and only those targets, at this time instead of the normal time during 601.2c. If the number of choices has a currently undefined value, such as “Choose X,” or a value that may change during the process of casting the spell, such as “If this spell was kicked, choose any number instead”, the player chooses any number of modes. When the spell's legality is checked (rule 601.2e), if the value is still undefined or the value does not match the choices originally made, the spell is illegal. If the player wishes to splice any cards onto the spell (see rule 702.46), they reveal those cards in their hand. If that player wishes to reprise any cards onto that spell (see rule 702.205), they exile those cards from their graveyard. If the player wishes to apply any Functions to that spell (see rule 111.10aj), they sacrifice those Functions. If the player wishes to apply any any modes from exiled cards with lucid (see rule 702.304), they put those cards into their owner's graveyard. They choose an order to apply those text-change effects to that spell. If the spell has alternative or additional costs that will be paid as it's being cast such as buyback or kicker costs (see rules 118.8 and 118.9), the player announces their intentions to pay any or all of those costs (see rule 601.2f). A player can't apply two alternative methods of casting or two alternative costs to a single spell. If the spell has a variable cost that will be paid as it's being cast (such as an {X} in its mana cost; see rule 107.3), the player announces the value of that variable. If the value of that variable is defined in the text of the spell by a choice that player would make later in the announcement or resolution of the spell, that player makes that choice at this time instead of that later time. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast includes hybrid mana symbols, the player announces the nonhybrid equivalent cost they intend to pay. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast includes Phyrexian mana symbols, the player announces whether they intend to pay 2 life or a corresponding colored mana cost for each of those symbols. Previously made choices (such as choosing to cast a spell with flashback from a graveyard or choosing to cast a creature with morph face down) may restrict the player's options when making these choices.

formal_source_nodes.name: 700.2a
formal_source_nodes.rule: Some modals printed with two options will allow a player to choose "both". If the spell has gained additional modes, such as from a card with lucid (see rule 702.304), only two modes can be chosen.

expected.name: Tunneler

subrules.rule: Tunneler is a static ability of some creatures. “Tunneler” means “As this creature enters, you may open the tunnels” and “As this creature becomes untapped, you may have it descend into the tunnels or exit the tunnels.”

subrules.name: 702.209b
subrules.rule: As a creature enters, if the tunnels are open, that creature's controller may have it descend into the tunnels.

subrules.name: 702.209c
subrules.rule: Creatures that are in the tunnels can only block and only be blocked by creatures that are in the tunnels.

subrules.name: 702.209d
subrules.rule: At the beginning of combat on each player's turn, if the tunnels are open and no creatures are in the tunnels, that player may close the tunnels.

expected.name: Chant

subrules.name: 702.223a
subrules.rule: Chant is a static ability that functions while a card is in your hand. “Chant [cost]” means “You may exile this card from your hand as you cast an instant or sorcery spell. If you do, that spell gains the text found within square brackets in this card’s rules text and you pay [cost] as an additional cost to cast that spell. You may cast this card as long as this card remains exiled.” Paying a card’s chant cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

subrules.name: 702.223b
subrules.rule: Some effect may allow a player to "add the chants" of cards to spells they cast. To do so, they choose the cards with chant that will add their chants. The spell gains the text found within the square brackets in those card's rules text, and that player pays [cost] as an additional cost to cast that spell. The chanting creatures will not be exiled.

subrules.name: 702.223c
subrules.rule: You can’t choose to use a chant ability if you can’t make the required choices (targets, etc.) for that card’s rules text. If you’re chanting more than one card onto a spell, exile them all at once and choose the order in which their effects will happen. The effects of the main spell must happen first.

subrules.name: 702.223d
subrules.rule: The spell has the characteristics of the main spell, plus the rules text found in the square brackets of each of the chanting cards. This is a text-changing effect (see rule 612, “Text-Changing Effects”). The spell doesn’t gain any other characteristics (name, mana cost, color, supertypes, card types, subtypes, etc.) of the chanting cards. Text gained by the spell that refers to a card by name refers to the spell on the stack, not the card from which the text was copied.

subrules.name: 702.223e
subrules.rule: Choose targets for the added text normally (see rule 601.2c). Note that a spell with one or more targets won’t resolve if all of its targets are illegal on resolution.

subrules.name: 702.223f
subrules.rule: The spell loses any chant changes once it leaves the stack for any reason.

formal_source_nodes.name: 601.2b
formal_source_nodes.rule: If the spell is modal, the player announces the mode choice (see rule 700.2). If the player making the mode choice needs to be targeted, the player casting the spell announces their choice of an appropriate player for each target required to make that choice, and only those targets, at this time instead of the normal time during 601.2c. If the number of choices has a currently undefined value, such as “Choose X,” or a value that may change during the process of casting the spell, such as “If this spell was kicked, choose any number instead”, the player chooses any number of modes. When the spell's legality is checked (rule 601.2e), if the value is still undefined or the value does not match the choices originally made, the spell is illegal. If the player wishes to splice any cards onto the spell (see rule 702.46), they reveal those cards in their hand. If that player wishes to chant any cards onto that spell (see rule 702.223), they exile those cards from their hand. They choose an order to apply those text-change effects to that spell. If the spell has alternative or additional costs that will be paid as it's being cast such as buyback or kicker costs (see rules 118.8 and 118.9), the player announces their intentions to pay any or all of those costs (see rule 601.2f). A player can't apply two alternative methods of casting or two alternative costs to a single spell. If the spell has a variable cost that will be paid as it's being cast (such as an {X} in its mana cost; see rule 107.3), the player announces the value of that variable. If the value of that variable is defined in the text of the spell by a choice that player would make later in the announcement or resolution of the spell, that player makes that choice at this time instead of that later time. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast includes hybrid mana symbols, the player announces the nonhybrid equivalent cost they intend to pay. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast includes Phyrexian mana symbols, the player announces whether they intend to pay 2 life or the corresponding colored mana cost for each of those symbols. Previously made choices (such as choosing to cast a spell with flashback from a graveyard or choosing to cast a creature with morph face down) may restrict the player's options when making these choices.

expected.name: Campaign Cards

subrules.rule: Each Campaign card has a striated text box containing a number of strategy symbols. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its type line is along the bottom of the card.
A strategy symbol is a keyword ability that represents one or more triggered abilities referred to as strategy abilities.

subrules.name: 740.2a
subrules.rule: A strategy symbol includes a number of flags, indicated here as “{f}.”

subrules.name: 740.2b
subrules.rule: “{f}, {f}—[Effect]” means the same as “{f}—[Effect]” and “{f}—[Effect].”

subrules.name: 740.2c
subrules.rule: Whenever a Campaign's controller attacks, they put a strategy counter on the Campaign.

subrules.name: 740.2d
subrules.rule: As a strategy counter is put on a Campaign, its controller triggers a strategy ability of that Campaign of their choice. That ability can't be triggered this way again as long as that counter remains on the Campaign.

subrules.name: 740.2e
subrules.rule: A Campaign’s final strategy number is the total number of strategy abilities it has. If a Campaign somehow has no strategy abilities, its final strategy number is 0.
Camapaigns use strategy counters to track their progress.

If the number of strategy counters on a Campaign permanent is greater than or equal to its final strategy number, and it isn't the source of a strategy ability that has triggered but not yet left the stack, that Campaigns's controller sacrifices it. This state-based action doesn't use the stack.

expected.reason: Adds strategy progress and a Campaign-specific final-strategy state-based sacrifice. Replacing it with an ordinary trigger or a Saga changes timing and identity.

expected.name: Discharge Cards
expected.reason: Permanent entry/gaining Discharge inherently creates and retains a spell copy in exile, an explicit exception to704.5e, with a linked removable-counter casting cost. This adds new copy/SBA/category rules.

expected.name: Discharge Cards

subrules.rule: Discharge cards have a two-part card frame, with a smaller frame inset within their text box.

The text that appears in the inset frame on the right defines alternative characteristics that the object may have while it’s a spell. The card’s normal characteristics appear as usual, although with a smaller text box on the left.

subrules.name: 743.2a
subrules.rule: The inset frame of a discharge card is called a “Discharge spell.” If a rule or effect refers to a card, spell, or permanent that has a Discharge spell, it refers to an object for which these alternative characteristics exist, even if the object currently doesn’t use them.

subrules.name: 743.2b
subrules.rule: The existence and values of these alternative characteristics are part of the object’s copiable values.

subrules.name: 743.2c
subrules.rule: Although discharge cards are printed with multiple sets of characteristics, each discharge card is only one card. For example, a player who has drawn or discarded a discharge card has drawn or discarded one card, not two.
Discharge cards can’t be cast using the alternative characteristics found within their inset frames. Rather, these characteristics are used to define characteristics of copies which may be cast.

subrules.name: 743.3a
subrules.rule: As a permanent with a Discharge spell enters or a permanent gains a Discharge, its controller creates a copy of the Discharge spell in exile, except that copy has only the characteristics of that permanent’s Discharge spell, ignoring other exceptions to the copying process that apply to that permanent. Those characteristics become the copy’s normal characteristics. This copy remains in exile for as long as the permanent remains on the battlefield and has the Discharge spell. This is an exception to rule 704.5e. For as long as the copy remains in exile, the permanent’s controller may cast the copy by removing a counter from the permanent in addition to paying the spell's other costs.

subrules.name: 743.3b
subrules.rule: If a Discharge spell is copied, the copy is also a Discharge spell. Any rule or effect that refers to a spell cast as a Discharge spell refers to the copy as well.
In every zone, a discharge card has only its normal characteristics.
If an effect instructs a player to choose a card name and the player wants to choose a discharge card’s alternative name, the player may do so.

expected.reason: Permanent entry/gaining Discharge inherently creates and retains a spell copy in exile, an explicit exception to704.5e, with a linked removable-counter casting cost. This adds new copy/SBA/category rules.

expected.rule: If a face-down permanent that was cast for its undercover cost would die, instead its controller exiles it face down. No player looks at or reveals the card as it's exiled. This is an exception to rules 400.6 and 707.9. The player who exiled it may look at the exiled card and may play it for as long as it remains exiled, but can't play it face down this way. If the exiled card leaves exile, becomes a new object (see rule 406.7), its owner leaves the game, or the game ends, the card must be revealed to all players.
